title: HUMAN-GUIDED FAIR CLASSIFICATION FOR NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING

bias_targets.methodology: Generating counterfactual sentence pairs by swapping gender identity markers (e.g., male, female, transgender) using word replacement, unsupervised style transfer, and GPT-3, then evaluating if toxicity classifiers yield identical predictions for both sentences (individual fairness).

Generating counterfactual sentence pairs by swapping racial and ethnic identity markers (e.g., Black, White, Asian, Latino) using word replacement, unsupervised style transfer, and GPT-3, then evaluating classifier consistency (individual fairness) and computing TPR/TNR gaps (group fairness).

Generating counterfactual sentence pairs by swapping religious identity markers (e.g., Christian, Muslim, Jewish, Hindu) using word replacement, unsupervised style transfer, and GPT-3, then evaluating individual fairness in toxicity classification.

Generating counterfactual sentence pairs by swapping sexual orientation markers (e.g., heterosexual, homosexual, bisexual) using word replacement, unsupervised style transfer, and GPT-3, then evaluating individual fairness in toxicity classification.

Training a group-presence classifier to detect mentions of physical, intellectual, and mental disabilities, and generating counterfactual statements to assess classification invariance across demographic perturbations.
